name: llm-prefill-decode-visualizer
description: Machine-readable index of every agent-facing endpoint on the LLM Prefill & Decode Speed Visualizer API. All endpoints return JSON (except /api/watch/rss.xml, which returns RSS XML), support CORS, require no auth, and are also served under the /v1/ prefix (replace /api/ with /v1/). Full request/response details: GET /api/spec (OpenAPI 3.1). Human + agent docs: /llms.txt.

endpoints.description: Run inference math (TTFT, TPOT, walltime, VRAM): ?model=singleTurn|speculative|batched|agentic|kvCache|flagged|cost plus parameters. No model param returns a self-describing capability list. Add dry_run=true to validate without executing.
endpoints.responseSchema: { id, inputs, warnings[], ttftSeconds, tpotMs, decodeSeconds, totalWalltimeSeconds, effectiveThroughputTokPerSec, prefillSharePct, decodeSharePct, schema_version }

endpoints.description: Batch up to 50 parameter sets in one round trip: {"batch": [{"model": ..., ...}]} (also accepted as "variants" or ?batch=[...] on GET). Per-item ok/error status; supports per-item dry_run.
endpoints.responseSchema: { batch: true, count, okCount, errorCount, results: [{ index, ok, result | error }] }

endpoints.description: Replay a computation or /api/best recommendation from its deterministic id (calc_<12 hex>). Ids are content hashes: re-send the original parameters and get verified:true; mismatches are rejected with the expected id.
endpoints.responseSchema: <original result> + { id, verified: true }

endpoints.description: Built-in hardware speed presets (RTX 4090, dual RTX 3090, M3 Ultra, Groq LPU, H100, RPi5…) and workload scenarios (RAG query, code generation) — feed as /api/compute inputs.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, hardware[{id, name, prefillSpeedTokPerSec, decodeSpeedTokPerSec, vramBandwidth, badge}], scenarios[{id, label, promptTokens, outputTokens}], schema_version }

endpoints.description: Combined weights + KV-cache VRAM from just an hfId (?hfId=&context=&quant=). Optional vramGb budget → fits flag + maxContextTokens; optional numTurns+tokensPerTurn → per-turn KV growth projection with first overflow turns. Also accepts POST with a JSON body.
endpoints.responseSchema: { inputs, model{architecture, resolutionSource}, weights{gb}, kvCache{bytesPerToken, gbAtContext, formula}, total{gb, breakdown}, contextWindow, fits, projection }

endpoints.description: Community-measured single-stream benchmark runs. Bare call = hardware-group summary; ?hardware=&model=&quant=&context_band=&limit=&cursor= filters return cursor-paginated runs sorted by decode speed desc.
endpoints.responseSchema: { snapshot, total, caveats[], items[{runId, modelFamily, hardwareKey, hwClass, engine, quantization, prefillTokPerSec, decodeTokPerSec, contextBand, ageDays, staleness, source}], has_more, next_cursor }

endpoints.description: Submit a community benchmark run for manual review. Required: model, quant, hardware, hwClass (discrete_gpu|unified|cpu_only), prefillTokPerSec, decodeTokPerSec. Sanity bounds + near-duplicate rejection; 202 = queued, never published immediately.
endpoints.requestSchema: { model, quant, hardware, hwClass, prefillTokPerSec, decodeTokPerSec, engine?, provenance?, submitter? }
endpoints.responseSchema: 202 { description, status: 'queued', reviewStatus, submissionId } · 400/409 { error, errors[] }

endpoints.description: Aggregated median + IQR + 95% bootstrap CI per hardware×model group (outlier-resistant). ?groupBy=hardware|model|quant regroups. Cursor-paginated; each item carries confidence + crossCheck + bestRun.
endpoints.responseSchema: { snapshot, total, caveats[], items[{key, runs, prefill{median, ci95, label}, decode{…}, engines[], confidence, crossCheck, bestRun}], has_more, next_cursor }

endpoints.description: Ranked answers: ?by=decode|prefill|cost plus filters (model, maxParamsB, quant, hwClass, fitCheck+contextLength). Responses carry a deterministic id replayable via /api/calc/{id}?endpoint=best. Also accepts POST.
endpoints.responseSchema: { id, rankedBy, snapshot, matchedRuns, caveats[], results[{hardware, hwClass, modelFamily, quantization, confidence, medianDecodeTokPerSec, medianDecodeCi95, pricing{}, power?, explain}] }

endpoints.description: Diff two measured runs (?runA=<id>&runB=<id>) or two constraint sets (?mode=whatif&a=<set>&b=<set>): deltas, ratios, feasible-set changes and headroom. Also accepts POST {mode,a,b} for what-if mode.
endpoints.responseSchema: { runA, runB, diff{…} } · what-if: { entered[], left[], headroom[] }

endpoints.description: Full comparable dataset as a downloadable file: ?format=csv (RFC 4180 with #-metadata preamble) or ?format=json (envelope with dataDictionary + runs array). The comparable subset is also listed at /api/runs?comparable=true.
endpoints.responseSchema: text/csv or application/json attachment

endpoints.description: One-call deployment recommendation: pass a workload spec (?model=<family>&contextLength=&concurrency=&maxTtftSeconds=&maxTpotMs=&maxVramGb=), get ranked rigs with VRAM-fit math, expected TTFT/TPOT from benchmark medians, confidence and meetsSlo flags. Also accepts POST with a JSON body.
endpoints.responseSchema: { workload, slo, matchedRuns, assumptions, recommendations[{hardware, vramFit, expected, confidence, meetsSlo, explain, source}] }

endpoints.description: Turn plain-language constraints into the canonical struct: ?q=self-hosted Qwen 27B at Q4 for 10 users under $1500 → constraints + ambiguities + ready-made sizingQuery. Deterministic regex/heuristics, no LLM.
endpoints.responseSchema: { input, recognizedCount, constraints{deployment, modelFamily, paramsB, quantization, contextLength, concurrency, budgetUsdMax, …}, ambiguities[{field, message}], sizingQuery }

endpoints.description: Versioned dataset snapshot IDs. Pin any data endpoint with ?snapshot=<id> for reproducible results; unknown/expired IDs fall back to current data with snapshot.served=false.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, current, snapshots[{id, createdAt, runCount}] }

endpoints.description: List registered hardware+model watch combos (never includes secrets or webhook URLs). POST creates a watch; DELETE ?id=&secret= removes one.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, maxWatches, totalWatches, watches[{watchId, label, model, hardware, quant, hasWebhook, createdAt}] }

endpoints.description: Create a watch for a hardware+model combo: {model?, hardware?, quant?, webhookUrl?} — at least one of model/hardware required. Returns 201 with one-time secret and a ready-made rssUrl (RSS needs no webhook).
endpoints.responseSchema: 201 { watchId, secret, rssUrl, matchingExistingRuns }

endpoints.description: Remove a watch: ?id=<watchId>&secret=<one-time secret from POST>. Secret also accepted as X-Watch-Secret header.
endpoints.responseSchema: 204 No Content

endpoints.description: RSS 2.0 feed of community runs for a watched combo — poll in any feed reader, no registration. Filters mirror GET /api/localmaxxing; newest matching runs first, max 50 items.
endpoints.responseSchema: application/rss+xml

endpoints.description: Cron-friendly webhook delivery: for each watch with a webhookUrl, POST unseen matching runs as a watch.new_runs payload. Set WATCH_DISPATCH_SECRET env var to require ?secret=. Also accepts POST.
endpoints.responseSchema: { dispatched, totalNewRuns, results[{watchId, newRuns, delivered}], schemaNote, previewPayload }

endpoints.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over Streamable HTTP JSON-RPC: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, ping. Tool calls proxy to the REST handlers above. Manifest at /.well-known/mcp.json.
endpoints.responseSchema: { jsonrpc: '2.0', id, result } (JSON-RPC 2.0)

endpoints.description: Full OpenAPI 3.1 spec with x-examples per operation — derive typed clients from this.
endpoints.responseSchema: OpenAPI 3.1 document

endpoints.description: Liveness probe + upstream data freshness ({ok, upstreamFreshness, cacheAge}). Human status page at /status.html.
endpoints.responseSchema: { ok, service, time, upstreamFreshness{status, fetchedAt, ageSeconds, ttlSeconds, rowCount, source}, cacheAge }

endpoints.description: One-shot machine-readable dump of the FULL run index (comparable AND batched/non-comparable). ?format=json|csv; ?comparable=all|true|false. JSON envelope carries schemaVersion, generatedAt, rowCount, totalRunCount, comparableFilter and a structured dataDictionary. Legacy alias: /api/export serves the same dump as a downloadable file.
endpoints.responseSchema: { schemaVersion, generatedAt, comparableFilter, rowCount, totalRunCount, comparableCount, dataDictionary[], runs[] }

endpoints.description: Machine-readable version report: service name, app version (package.json), the wire schema_version stamped on every JSON response (single spelling), generatedAt and links to /api/versions, /api/spec, CHANGELOG-API.md and CHANGELOG.json.
endpoints.responseSchema: { service, version, generatedAt, links{} } + universal schema_version stamp

endpoints.description: Version discovery: every served URL prefix (/api, /v1) with its wire schema_version, lifecycle status (current|deprecated), canonical flag, deprecatedAt and sunset. Deprecated prefixes carry Deprecation/Sunset headers on every response.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, generatedAt, current, versions[]{prefix, schema_version, status, canonical, deprecatedAt, sunset}, links{} }

endpoints.description: This index — machine-readable discovery document listing every agent-facing surface with methods, kind and descriptions. Static, CDN-cached 1h.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, generatedAt, schema_version, surfaces[] }

endpoints.description: Agent-friendly wrapper over the same inference math as /api/compute. GET with ?model= plus params, or POST {"batch":[...]} (up to 50 sets). Flat self-describing envelope with resolved inputs and a deterministic calc id. Bare call returns the capability catalog.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, endpoint, generatedAt, scenario?, inputs, id, ...mathFields, warnings[], schema_version }

endpoints.description: Agent-friendly wrapper around the raw community run search (same data as MCP search_runs / GET /api/localmaxxing). Flat per-run records with tok/s speeds, freshness stamps, echoed filters and cursor pagination. Filters: ?hardware=, ?model=, ?quant=, ?context_band=, ?max_age=, ?limit=, ?cursor=, ?snapshot=.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, endpoint, generatedAt, filters, results[], pagination{}, schema_version }

endpoints.description: Agent-friendly loader for the built-in workload scenario presets (same SCENARIO_PRESETS as the UI quick-start chips and /api/presets). No ?id= returns the directory of every valid scenario; ?id=<preset> returns token counts plus derived totalTokens/prefillShare and next-hop pointers. Unknown ids return 400 with valid ids.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, endpoint, generatedAt, scenarios[] | scenario{ id, label, promptTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens, prefillShare, nextSteps{} } }

endpoints.description: Agent-readable data-freshness + confidence report wrapping groupFreshness/staleness tiers, confidenceFor/aggregate and upstream cache state. Filters: ?hardware=, ?model=, ?quant=, ?context_band=, ?max_age=, ?groupBy=hardware|model|hardwareModel, ?snapshot=. Alias: /api/agent/confidence.json.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, generatedAt, filters, cache{}, dataset{}, groups[], summary{} }

endpoints.description: Alias for GET /api/agent/freshness.json — identical handler and response shape.
endpoints.responseSchema: same as /api/agent/freshness.json

endpoints.description: RFC 9457 problem-type documentation for every error code advertised in problem+json `type` URIs (/problems/<slug>, slug = lowercased CODE with _ -> -). No argument returns the registry index; ?code=<slug|CODE> or /api/problems/<slug> returns { code, slug, type, title, status, description, spec }. Unknown codes return 404 with the available slugs.
endpoints.responseSchema: { description, codes[] } index, or per-code { code, slug, type, title, status, description, spec }
